faq: Which booking tools do you use?
Calendly, Cal.com, Acuity, Square Appointments, Google Calendar booking pages and your site's own booking app. We pick one that fits your needs, and you pay the tool plan directly.
Can people book without making an account?
Yes, and we recommend it. A booking only needs a name, email and the questions you choose, so there is little to put people off.
Can I collect a payment when someone books?
On Premium, yes, using your own payment provider such as Stripe or PayPal. We never see card details, as payments run through the provider's secure form.
What if I work across time zones?
The tool shows each person your free times in their own time zone, and we test that it does. We also set minimum notice, so no one books you for ten minutes from now.

desc:
Online booking page setup for leads means giving every enquiry a page where they pick a free time for a call, visit or consultation. Ecom Swift LLC builds that page in your own scheduling tool, connects your calendar and tests the full booking before launch.

## What is an online booking page for leads?

An online booking page is a web page that shows your real free times and lets a visitor reserve one without sending a single email. It reads your calendar, so only open slots appear, and it writes the new appointment back to the same calendar. The visitor gets a confirmation, and you get a booking with the details already filled in.

For lead generation, this page replaces the slow exchange of "what time suits you?" messages. The person who just showed interest can act while the interest is fresh.

## Why scheduling by email loses leads

Every message in a scheduling thread gives the lead a chance to get distracted, find another provider or simply forget. A reply that arrives the next morning may already be too late. Even when the thread works, it eats your time, and it often ends with a double booking or a missed time zone.

A booking page removes the waiting. The lead sees what is available, chooses, and receives proof that the slot is theirs. You stop acting as a human diary and spend that time on the work itself.

## How a good booking page improves your results

A booking page lowers the effort needed to say yes. Fewer steps between "I am interested" and "it is in my calendar" means more of your enquiries turn into real conversations. Reminder emails and texts then reduce no-shows, because people are told about the appointment again before it happens.

Intake questions help too. When the lead tells you what they need before the call, you arrive prepared and the conversation starts further along. Results still depend on your offer, your traffic and how quickly you can meet people, but the page removes one common point of loss.

## What a great booking page includes

- A clear page title and short line explaining what the meeting is and who it is for.
- Meeting lengths that match the real work, with buffer time between appointments.
- Availability rules for working hours, days off, holidays and minimum notice.
- A connected calendar that blocks times you are already busy.
- A few intake questions that help you prepare without feeling like an exam.
- Confirmation emails that state the time, the place or video link and what to bring.
- Reminder messages sent before the meeting.
- Cancel and reschedule links, so changes do not need a phone call.
- Correct time zone handling for visitors in other regions.
- A page that loads quickly and works on a phone.

## What we do

We start by choosing the right tool for your situation, using the booking feature of your current website platform or CRM where it fits, or a dedicated scheduling tool in your own account. We then connect your calendar, set meeting types, lengths, buffers and working hours, and write the page text and confirmation email in your voice.

Depending on the package, we add intake questions, reminder emails and texts, cancel and reschedule links, team calendars, paid or deposit bookings, and a connection that sends booking data to your CRM. We embed or link the page on your site, then run test bookings from a phone and a computer, including a cancellation, to confirm that every message and calendar entry is correct.

## What to do and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Offer only meeting types you can deliver well.
- Keep intake questions to the ones you will really read.
- Allow a little buffer time between meetings.
- Show the booking button wherever a lead first reaches out.
- Test the page yourself as if you were a new customer.

**Avoid:**
- Leaving every hour of the week open.
- Asking for long forms before the visitor has booked anything.
- Forgetting to connect a personal or second calendar that holds busy times.
- Sending confirmations that leave out the place or video link.
- Hiding the page behind a menu so that visitors cannot find it.

## Who this service is for

This service suits consultants, coaches and agencies who spend part of every week arranging calls by email. It also fits local service businesses such as clinics, studios and installers who want visitors to request a visit or estimate time. A small team that needs several people to take bookings from one page is another good match.

## What we need from you

Tell us what meetings you offer, how long each lasts and which hours you want to be bookable. Send us the calendar you use and any tool you already pay for, along with the wording or questions you would like on the page. We never need your passwords. Access is given to us as a collaborator, staff or team user in your own scheduling tool and calendar, and you keep full ownership from the first day.
